scope: Read-only certified operand interval filter for native AABB point containment. Candidate remains subject to focused correctness, runtime, output, allocation and size gates.
preconditions: The existing AABB API requires min <= max. Display-preview policy does not enter this filter. Fully rational inputs retain the existing borrowed-rational predicate.

interval_proof.notation: For each axis, a in [a0,a1] is the minimum, b in [b0,b1] the maximum, and p in [p0,p1] the point.
interval_proof.outside: p1 < a0 implies p < a; p0 > b1 implies p > b. Either certifies a box miss.
interval_proof.inside: p0 >= a1 and p1 <= b0 imply a <= p <= b. This must hold on both axes to certify containment.
interval_proof.fallback: Any missing cache or unresolved overlap falls through to the existing Hyperlimit predicate. Read-only cached_rational_interval(-32) does not initiate refinement and rejects aborted non-rational values.
interval_proof.boundaries: Weak inequalities are allowed only when entire closed intervals establish containment. Overlapping uncertain endpoint intervals do not imply equality.

tests.integer_oracle: 120 integer points around [-2,3] x [-5,7], translated by sin(7)+sqrt(53) and pi, multiplied by 1, -3, 1e400 or 1e-400; two policy families and cold/warm query sequences, 1920 containment queries. Expected membership is calculated in the original integer coordinates.
tests.boundary_and_close_gap: Both endpoints and points 1e-40 inside/outside either endpoint under both policies. The 32-bit interval filter must decline; the original correlated exact predicate must return the oracle answer with Certified certainty.
tests.aborted_cache: A warmed non-rational coordinate proves containment before abort and is rejected by the filter after its abort flag is set.
tests.additional: Existing exact AABB construction, reversed near-zero corners, singleton separation, native arc extrema, integration AABB cases and policy-budget regressions are included.
